evidence: REACHABILITY. Every graded capability is reachable from the seed plus the pinned runtime. Runtime: environment/Dockerfile installs express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally on node:22-bookworm-slim with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules; tests/Dockerfile installs the same two versions with the same NODE_PATH, and test.sh launches node with env -i PATH/NODE_PATH/HOME/PORT/DB_PATH as uid 65534, exactly the environment hireops_rules.md section 8 (lines 196-202) and integration.md describe. Sessions/cookies, password checks, polling or SSE need only Node built-ins plus Express (rules line 123 allows polling/SSE/sockets, so no ws package is required). Network is public (task.toml network_mode public for both phases); instruction.md line 13 allows CDN fonts/scripts and forbids only an external data backend, which matches the project delivery profile. SEED vs GRADED FACTS (parsed): Platform Engineer Applied = Greta Lindqvist(1), Ade Bello(2), Marco Rossi(3), Screen = Priya Nair(1), Samuel Ortiz(2) and note on APP-101 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' match hro_restart/protocol Z exactly. APP-101 has 120 messages, per-conversation timestamps strictly increasing with no ties (paging 30/90-60-30-0 is well defined). Lena (USR-CAN3) read_count 2 of APP-301's 3 messages and the 3rd is from USR-REC3, so the protocol's 'Lena starts with 1 unread' follows from rules lines 151-153 and 206-208. Noor's read_count 119 leaves only her own 120th message, consistent with 'own messages are never unread'. thread_page_size 30 and candidate_status_labels in the seed match rules section 7 and hro_candidate_view. Candidate accounts own seeded applications (Noor: APP-101, APP-302; Tomas: APP-201; Lena: APP-301 rejected with rejected_from/reject_reason), so every candidate leg has data. UNAMBIGUITY of graded rules: one-step moves (rules 47-48), reject not from Hired with non-blank reason (49-50), reopen only to the rejected-from stage clearing the reason (51), interview places 1-50 whole number (28), whole-set place counting and board-order arrival defined explicitly as 'by stage in the order listed above, then by place' (89-92), undo restoring stage+place and the rejection reason a move removed (96-100, which also makes clear a reopening is an undoable move), refusal when any card of that move was moved/re-ordered/rejected/reopened by anyone, single use, superseded by a later move, notes excluded (98-100); stale detection by a per-card version 'that changes whenever the card moves' (77-80), so protocol C's ABA replay (F returned to Applied by Mei, old request replayed) has one reading; status codes 401/403/404 (21-23) and the 404-for-candidates rule is the only 404 case, matching hro_refusal_status/hro_thread_access; unread definition (151-160) and seen definition incl. observer exclusion (164-166); conversation paging and place retention (144-147); drafts per person/conversation/browser surviving reload and ended session (170-175); live updates within 15 s preserving typing, focus, open card/conversation, scroll (117-123). Roles: HM 'only among Interview, Offer and Hired, including re-ordering ... reject from Interview or Offer and reopen a card rejected from one of those' (70-72) maps one-to-one onto hro_mgr_late_stages/hro_mgr_early_refused. RUN EVIDENCE (scripted golden, not a configured judge run): raw-evidence-index artifacts verified by hash; workspace.json shows all 25 groups passed against the frozen solution bytes in the verifier image as uid 65534 with a real restart, including stale-move naming (3,15), bulk/undo semantics (6,7,9,10,16), unread/seen (12,13,19), paging and place retention (18), session-ended draft resume (21) and restart without reseed (23). This demonstrates the brief is achievable in the provided runtime; it is not an Oracle, judge or model score. NOTES (each P3, no second reading that a conforming app would plausibly take and be graded down for; reported per the row's 'report every ambiguity' duty): (N1) rules line 32 'The email must look like an email address' leaves edge strings (e.g. 'a@b' without a dot) open; protocol S says only 'an invalid address' and the judge picks it. Suggest stating one example of a refused address or telling the judge to use an obviously invalid value such as 'not-an-email'. (N2) rules line 98 'if any of those cards has been ... re-ordered since' could be read as including a passive index shift caused by another card's re-order; line 77 ('a version that changes whenever the card moves') and hro_undo_conflict's 'changes only a different card' point to the direct-action reading, and protocol B(12) re-orders Y at the top of Screen so A2's place is not shifted. (N3) Drafts across a deliberate sign-out: instruction line 7 says 'get signed out'; a privacy-minded app might clear drafts on explicit sign-out. The rules (170-175 'belongs to that person ... on that browser', 'Anyone else who signs in on that browser sees none of them', 'Sending clears the draft'; notes 'kept ... until it is saved', 104-106) only make sense if drafts outlive a sign-out, so hro_pol_session_resume's sign-out legs follow the dominant reading. (N4) Ungraded unspecified items, harmless because both readings pass every criterion: whether a hiring manager can view boards/notes/activity of other jobs; whether a reject or a hand re-order counts as an undoable 'move' (no protocol step undoes either); observer unread totals. (N5) Workbook conflict recorded, not a task defect: the Internal Quality Checks annotation for row 6 says 'with no network', while the shipped Quality Checks row and the SKILL delivery profile say network is public; the current project profile governs. OUT-OF-ROW observation for the owner (criteria/tool feasibility rows, not graded here): if an app carries its session in an Authorization header rather than a cookie, a replay that copies the captured request 'exactly' into another person's session could carry Rafael's credential; prompt.md asks for the stated session, but it does not say to substitute that session's own auth header. Try-broken / try-conforming: a broken app that applies the stale replay because F is genuinely back in Applied (precondition = from-stage) would correctly fail hro_stale_refused under the explicit version rule; a conforming app using SSE, header tokens, or a different route layout remains within the brief (instruction line 13, rules lines 3-5, app_context 'any route layout'), subject only to the out-of-row replay note above.
